details:
A friend encouraged me to suggest this, so here I am.
Understandably VRChat has a LARGE population of younger users. A lot them younger than the games intended audience. But there is also a large adult population on VRChat.
Any game that has adults and minors openly interacting with each other will be hard to moderate, this is understandable. But I constantly see literal children being exposed to content they should not be. Adult topic conversations, skimply dressed avatars, drunk people, etc. I've also known many minors that have been taken advantage of by adults in the game.
Children should be allowed to play the game just as much as adults are. But I think there seriously needs to be a barrier put in place to PROTECT minors, but also to provide comfortability for adults. Worlds like FBT Haven and Drinking Night are brilliant adult themed worlds. But they are easily accessed by minors. Not to mention minors can easily access avatars that are stylised towards adults (such as avatars containing weapons or skimpy clothing). 
These things should be removed. Adults should be allowed their content in VRChat as much as minors are. I think we should have some form of access pass.
Those of you who may have come to VRChat from playing IMVU years ago, you'll know that it's a desktop chat game with avatars. They introduced an access pass, that restricted adult content. All content (assets, worlds, avatars) were restricted if NSFW in nature (themes of a sexual or violent nature, etc). It could be that the upload process via Unity (with an updated SDK) could add an option to mark something as access pass only. Minors would not be able to enter access pass worlds, and any access pass avatars could be replaced for them with a fallback avatar much like you have put in place for the Quest. 
I would happily pay $5 for an access pass of sorts. You could set up a page on the website that requires purchase with a card and also proof of identification to make sure kids aren't just gonna use their parents card. 
People will probably get pissed that you're locking content between like, a $5 dollar pass (honestly I wouldn't charge higher than this) but at the end of the day, it is our responsibility as adults to protect minors from adult content. If you're an adult and you don't care, you're part of the issue. These are children and we need to protect them when they are online. They shouldn't be exposed to NSFW stuff. They should be playing friendly games and making friends.
title: NSFW content
